sentences: Hereditary graph classes can be specified by finitely many forbidden induced subgraphs.
The question asks whether graph isomorphism on such a class can have complexity intermediate between polynomial time and general graph-isomorphism completeness.
The source establishes broad classifications and resolves most two-forbidden-pattern cases.
Results for forbidden ordinary subgraphs do not immediately extend to induced exclusions.
The project seeks a dichotomy explaining whether a finite structural prohibition always makes isomorphism substantially easier or leaves its full general difficulty intact.
